title: Observation and interpretation
paragraphs: An observer can record a school, workshop, or military facility, but deciding what that institution means requires comparison. Was its success due to equipment, financing, legislation, trained personnel, or something less visible? Such questions help explain why reports from reform-era missions could become politically charged. They offered possibilities without resolving which changes were feasible or desirable in Korea.

The language used to describe foreign institutions mattered. Familiar concepts were sometimes stretched to accommodate unfamiliar organizations. Translation was not only linguistic; it was a negotiation over how to fit a different system into existing categories of thought.
